about.title: Vallejo Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Sonoma Boulevard and Tennessee Street carry a lot of Vallejo's daily traffic, and I-80 funnels commuters through the city morning and evening. In 2025, public collision records show Vallejo logged 439 injury collisions, with 610 people hurt and 19 lives lost. Those numbers are simply the record, but behind each one is someone sorting out medical bills, a damaged car, and an insurance adjuster who calls before the soreness has even set in. That early stretch matters. Photos of the scene, the other driver's information, witness contacts, and your own medical records all help establish what happened. What tends to hurt a claim is talking to the other side's insurer on a recorded line before you understand your rights. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Vallejo residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Talk to an Insurer in Vallejo

items.title: The clock is shorter than you might think
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but if a city, county, or state vehicle was involved, a claim may need to be filed in as little as six months. Knowing which deadline applies early keeps your options open.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover even if you share some of the blame; your award is simply reduced by your percentage. Insurers sometimes overstate your share, which is one reason to have someone reviewing the evidence on your behalf.

items.title: Your pain and disruption count, and they are not capped
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages in ordinary car accident cases, meaning pain, lost sleep, and time away from your life are all part of the picture. An attorney in our network works on contingency, so you pay nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise to hold off until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shrink your claim, even when you are being honest. A short, polite decline is enough.

items.question: I was rear-ended on I-80 near Vallejo during Friday evening traffic. Does it matter where the crash happened?
items.answer: Location matters mainly for evidence and jurisdiction. A crash on I-80 is typically handled by the California Highway Patrol rather than Vallejo police, so your collision report will come from a different agency. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. are when reported crashes in Vallejo tend to cluster, which can mean more witnesses and more traffic camera footage worth preserving quickly.

items.question: How much does it cost to be connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and there is no charge to be matched with an independent personal injury attorney. The attorneys in our network handle car accident cases on contingency, so legal fees come out of a recovery rather than your pocket, and if there is no recovery there is no fee.
